jobs.description:
Attention: Kapitus is aware that individuals posing as recruiters may be communicating with job seekers about supposed positions with Kapitus. Kapitus has received reports that the content and method of communication can vary, but messages may contain requests for payment (e.g., fees for equipment or training) and/or for sensitive financial information.

Kapitus will never ask a candidate for employment for payment or financial information during the initial application or interview process. All open positions are posted in location specific employment portals available at www.kapitus.com/careers   All legitimate Kapitus job postings on employment sites will direct candidates to complete an application through these portals before completion of the hiring process.

Candidates with additional questions or concerns regarding any recruiting communications or Kapitus’ recruiting process in general should email recruiting@kapitus.com

Please note: This position is 100% remote for candidates residing in Virginia. Candidates residing in Maryland and Washington, DC are also encouraged to apply and must be willing to work a hybrid schedule from our Arlington, VA office.

Kapitus has helped small and midsize businesses access capital for two decades, funding roughly $2 billion to date and building toward $6 billion and beyond. We originate, decision, fund, and service financing every day across a growing set of products and partner channels. As we scale, we are investing in the technology foundation that growth depends on, and we are creating our first dedicated Enterprise Architect role to lead it.

This is a build-and-shape role, not a maintain role. You will define the target-state architecture for the entire lending lifecycle, stand up the architecture practice that keeps it coherent, and sequence the modernization that unlocks the next phase of growth. You will work shoulder to shoulder with engineering, product, data, and security leaders, and your decisions will reach the platform that moves real money for real businesses.

What You Will Do:

• Own the end-to-end architecture. Produce and maintain a living, current, AI-crawlable map of how a deal flows from lead through decisioning, funding, servicing, and collections, and the systems, data stores, integrations, and owners behind it. Make it the single reference the whole organization trusts.

• Set the target state and sequence the path to it. Define the modernization roadmap, including the core-platform runtime uplift, decoupling decisioning from the core, the move toward a modern lending core, and the environments and infrastructure-as-code that let change ship safely. Sequence the work against the product roadmap so each initiative unblocks a business outcome.

• Establish the canonical data model. Define Kapitus-owned data models for the core decisioning inputs (credit bureau, cash flow, KYB), and a vendor-adapter layer so data providers plug in behind a stable internal contract. This removes single-vendor lock-in and enables failover and champion-challenger testing.

• Integrate the data and AI architecture, and keep it coherent. Partner closely with the Chief Data and AI Officer's organization so the data platform, the analytics and reporting products, the cross-team decisioning-data pipeline, and the machine-learning and model-deployment lifecycle fit cleanly into the enterprise architecture. Hold the operational-versus-analytical data split (real-time to the transactional store, analytical to the warehouse), define the ownership boundaries and contracts where data, engineering, and product meet so nothing sits orphaned between organizations, and maintain how that domain fits the overall picture as it evolves.

• Lead integration and event-driven architecture. Shape the API and eventing standards (REST, webhooks, event buses), the partner-API contract, and the middleware that connects Salesforce, the core platform, AWS services, and third parties.

• Design for security and resilience from the start. Make authentication, secrets management, least-privilege, audit logging, disaster recovery, high availability, and observability first-class attributes of every design, in a regulated-lending context.

• Stand up architecture governance. Run a lightweight, respected practice: architecture principles, decision records (ADRs) with real trade-off analysis, a design-review gate, and build-versus-buy and total-cost-of-ownership discipline. Keep it enabling, not bureaucratic.

• Partner, do not dictate. Bring product, engineering, the data and AI organization, and security into architecture decisions early through joint, rolling planning, and translate technical choices into business terms for executives and into clear guidance for engineers.

• Govern responsible AI enablement. Shape the guardrails and standards for AI-assisted development and for model deployment and governance, in partnership with the data and security organizations.

• Raise the bar across teams. Mentor engineering managers and technical leads, grow architectural thinking across the group, and leave the organization stronger than you found it.

What We’re Looking For:

• 10+ years experience in software engineering and architecture, several of them as an enterprise or solution architect owning complex, high-volume transactional systems end to end.

• Deep cloud-native architecture on AWS: containers and serverless, event-driven patterns, API management, relational and NoSQL data stores, and the security and cost controls around them.

• Strong data and analytics architecture: canonical and semantic models, warehouse and lakehouse patterns (for example Snowflake), the operational-versus-analytical data split, integration and adapter patterns, and comfort operating across the seam where a data organization and engineering meet.

• A track record modernizing legacy systems in production, including strangler and incremental-migration approaches that avoid big-bang risk.

• Security-and-compliance-by-design instincts, ideally in a regulated industry such as lending, fintech, banking, or insurance.

• Exceptional cross-functional influence: you build architecture with people, earn trust across product and engineering, and communicate clearly up to the board and down to the keyboard.

• A pragmatic, outcome-first mindset: you sequence to business value, make the call when evidence is sufficient, and document the why.

Nice to Haves:

• Salesforce platform architecture at scale, and experience with a modern lending or core-banking platform (for example Mambu or similar).

• Runtime and framework modernization (for example PHP major-version uplift), and microservice decomposition of a monolith.

• Credit-decisioning ecosystems: bureau and data vendors (Experian, LexisNexis, Plaid, and cash-flow providers), and model deployment and model-risk governance.

• Familiarity with AI-assisted development tooling and guardrails, and with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform or OpenTofu).

• A recognized architecture framework (for example TOGAF) used as a tool.

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year:

• A socialized, trusted end-to-end architecture map and a system-and-ownership inventory the whole organization uses, including during incidents.

• An approved target-state architecture and a sequenced modernization roadmap tied to the product plan and the funding case.

• A canonical data model and vendor-adapter standard adopted on the decisioning path, with a clear route to vendor failover.

• A running architecture practice: principles, decision records, and a design-review gate that engineers value.

• The data and AI domain integrated into the enterprise architecture, with the data-to-engineering seams, ownership, and contracts defined and agreed with the Chief Data and AI Officer's team.

• A measurable drop in architecture-driven incidents and rework, and faster, safer delivery of committed initiatives.

Kapitus Total Rewards Package Includes:

• Competitive Salary Rangeof $117,800-$189,000 annually. Kapitus is providing this as a good faith salary range to comply with applicable law. The applicant’s final salary will depend on a number of factors including the applicant’s geographic location, skills, and experience

• Annual Incentive Compensation Eligibility – Up to 10% annually

• Health Insurance: Comprehensive medical, dental, and employer-paid vision plans through UnitedHealthcare (UHC), with various coverage levels available to meet the needs of our employees and their families. Additional perks through UHC include: Sweat Equity, free subscription to the Calm App, UHC rewards, Real Appeal, and Quit For Life.

• Flexible Spending Account: Set aside pre-tax dollars from your paycheck to pay for qualified out-of-pocket medical, dental, vision, pharmacy or dependent care expenses.

• Lifestyle Spending Account: Employer sponsored post-tax benefits that allow reimbursement for expenses related to physical, mental and financial well-being.

• 100% Company Paid Insurances: Kapitus fully covers the cost of basic short-term and long-term disability insurance, as well as vision insurance, ensuring our employees have comprehensive protection without any personal expense.

• Voluntary Insurance: Supplemental life insurance as well as enhanced short- and long-term disability coverage are available through Mutual of Omaha, providing additional security for our employees. Additionally, Colonial Accident and Hospitalization insurances are also available, offering further protection against unforeseen events.

• Paid Maternity and Parental Leave: Beyond state-mandated leave policies, Kapitus provides company-paid maternity and parental leave, supporting our employees during important family milestones.

• Commuter Benefits: We offer pre-tax benefits on parking and commuter expenses to cover travel to and from work.

• LifeBalance Program: Enhance your lifestyle with our LifeBalance membership, which offers discounts on outdoor activities, the arts, health, and fitness. Additional benefits include: Pet and car insurance discounts. Financial services such as LegalShield. Relaxation and stress management tools.

• Plum Benefits Discount Program: Access exclusive discounts on shows, travel, car rentals, and more, enriching your personal and family life.

• Tuition Reimbursement: Pursue further education with up to $5,000 annually in tuition reimbursement, plus opportunities to attend relevant conferences and career development events. Managed through our LSA plan, Kapitus Academy.

About Kapitus:

We invest in every business owner’s story and we are dedicated to building lasting relationships to champion their goals. jobs.title: Senior Strategist
jobs.description:
Who We Are: LINK is a fast-growing Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB) that leverages human-centered design to support strategy, innovation, communication, change, and branding within the federal government and adjacent industry partners. At LINK, we partner with engineers, futurists, and thought leaders to untangle complexity, discover opportunity, and communicate clearly with visual stories.

Let us be your partners in change.

Location: We are actively hiring in the Washington, D.C. area.

About the Opportunity

LINK is looking for a Senior Strategist with a strong background in Communication to join our dynamic team. You will interface directly with clients to understand their unique challenges, provide consultative strategies and executive-level solutions, distill narratives from client-provided content, and collaborate with the creative team to execute visual products that align with the client’s brand, industry, and culture.

In this role, you will work with colleagues across the organization to uncover meaningful insights, build game-changing strategies, and deliver tailored solutions. Your expertise in Strategic Communications will play a pivotal role in driving LINK's business growth and delivering high-quality, client-focused outcomes.

The ideal candidate will have extensive experience working directly with clients, extracting key insights, and leading collaborative initiatives to achieve impactful results. This is an exciting opportunity to bring together creative and strategic expertise to contribute to LINK’s continued success.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communication, Business, Public Policy, English, or a related field.

• 10+ years of experience in strategic communications, consulting, public affairs, organizational transformation, program management, strategy, or a related field.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

• Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with clients and influence stakeholders at multiple levels of an organization.

• Strong strategic thinking, analytical problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.

• Experience facilitating executive-level discussions, workshops, and strategic planning efforts.

• Ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable plans.

• Interest in visual storytelling, data visualization, and communicating abstract concepts through compelling narratives.

• Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and attention to detail.

• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing executive-level presentations and strategic deliverables.

• Demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, exercise sound judgment, and lead work in complex, fast-paced environments.

• Extensive experience operating in ambiguous environments and exercising sound judgment with incomplete information.

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct experience in public affairs or strategic communications supporting the U.S. Navy, preferably within a headquarters, command, fleet, or other Navy organization.

• Demonstrated experience developing and executing communications strategies in support of Navy priorities, initiatives, or operations.

• Familiarity with Navy organizational structures, stakeholder environments, and military communication protocols is preferred.

• Experience developing messaging and communication products for senior military leaders, federal government stakeholders, and diverse public audiences is preferred.

Responsibilities

Client Partnership & Strategic Advisory

• Serves as a trusted advisor to clients by framing complex challenges, identifying opportunities, and translating ambiguity into actionable strategies and recommendations.

• Partners directly with client stakeholders to define missions, visions, strategic goals, and measurable KPIs/OKRs aligned to enterprise priorities.

• Leads strategic planning efforts, including executive workshops, stakeholder engagements, scenario planning activities, and initiative prioritization efforts.

• Conducts and oversees research, stakeholder interviews, benchmarking efforts, and current-state assessments to inform strategic recommendations.

• Synthesizes complex information into clear findings, strategic insights, and executive-level recommendations.

• Identifies opportunities to create tangible business value and helps shape follow-on work that supports client success and long-term engagement growth.

• Provides strategic guidance that helps clients make informed decisions and navigate organizational complexity.

Communication Strategy, Storytelling & Execution

• Translates complex ideas into compelling strategic narratives, executive-level presentations, communication strategies, and decision-support products.

• Develops messaging frameworks that align leadership vision, organizational priorities, and stakeholder needs.

• Designs content structures, information hierarchies, and storytelling approaches that communicate complex concepts clearly and effectively.

• Collaborates with creative teams to develop high-quality visual products that support strategic objectives and audience understanding.

• Establishes quality standards for strategic deliverables and provides guidance to team members to ensure consistency and excellence.

• Leads development of executive-ready materials that support decision-making, alignment, and organizational action.

Change Management & Organizational Transformation

• Develops and implements change management strategies, including stakeholder engagement plans, communications strategies, change impact assessments, and adoption roadmaps.

• Designs governance frameworks, operating models, and implementation approaches that support successful transformation efforts.

• Facilitates cross-functional working sessions that drive alignment, accelerate decision-making, and address organizational resistance.

• Establishes feedback mechanisms and performance measures that support continuous improvement and long-term success.

• Monitors progress, evaluates outcomes, and refines approaches based on stakeholder feedback and organizational needs.

Team Development & Leadership

• Mentors teammates through coaching, knowledge sharing, and constructive feedback.

• Models LINK values and contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture.

• Shares tools, approaches, and lessons learned that improve the quality and consistency of work across engagements.

Work Schedule

• Ad hoc on-site work with the client

• Full time, 40 hours per week

• Some travel required to attend relevant events and conferences, and participate in LINK team events

Salary: LINK is committed to offering competitive compensation. While the salary range for this position is $112,000 - $151,000, your final offer may be adjusted based on factors such as experience and location.

Benefits:

• $100 monthly internet/cell phone stipend

• $150 monthly commuter stipend for eligible participants

• LINK sponsored healthcare benefits including medical, dental, vision

• Company-paid Short Term Disability Insurance

• 401K with employer contribution of up to 4%

• 11 Federal Holidays per year

• 15 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) per year

• Paid Holiday Time Off (Christmas Eve through the New Year)

• Annual bonus plan participation

• Annual profit sharing participation

• $2,000 Learning and Development program reimbursement

• Technology package that includes a LINK-owned MacBook Pro, monitor, mouse and keyboard

LINK is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable state, local, and federal law.

If you are unable to complete this application due to a disability, contact Human Resources to ask for an accommodation or an alternative application process.

jobs.title: Compliance Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Us

At The Pharmacy Hub, we collaborate with pharmaceutical brands, manufacturers, health brands, telemedicine providers, and healthcare companies to deliver essential products directly to patients. Our expertise allows us to seamlessly distribute pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and other healthcare products to consumers, ensuring greater accessibility and convenience.

Position Summary

The Compliance Coordinator will directly support the Compliance Officer with the coordination and execution of compliance projects across pharmacy operations. This person will conduct regulatory research, support investigations, maintain documentation, track deadlines, and proactively follow up on pending items. They will work with Pharmacy, Quality, Operations, IT, HR, and the Licensing Specialist. Success in this role means accurate documentation, timely completion of delegated tasks, early identification of issues, and consistent follow-through with minimal supervision.

Core Responsibilities

Compliance Project Coordination (35%)

• Maintain a centralized tracker of compliance projects, deadlines, responsible parties, and pending items; provide reminders and regular status updates to the Compliance Officer.

• Coordinate delegated tasks across departments, follow up on outstanding requests, and promptly escalate delays or compliance concerns

Regulatory Research and Preparation of Findings (20%)

• Research pharmacy regulatory requirements using authoritative sources and prepare clear summaries for the Compliance Officer’s review.

• Review records and workflows for completeness and potential compliance gaps, and communicate findings to the Compliance Officer.

Documentation, SOP Support, Reports, and Records Management (15%)

• Draft correspondence, reports, procedures, forms, presentations, and meeting summaries for review and approval.

• Support SOP development and implementation with the SOP coordinator, including document control, version tracking, and acknowledgment records.

• Protect confidential information and maintain accurate, traceable records.

Investigation Support, Evidence Collection, and Corrective Action Tracking (15%)

• Support compliance investigations by collecting records, organizing evidence, preparing timelines, documenting findings, and tracking corrective actions.

• Track corrective and preventive actions, training requirements, and supporting evidence through completion.

Audit and Inspection Preparation (10%)

• Organize documentation for inspections, audits, regulatory requests, and client compliance inquiries.

• Coordinate with IT and software vendors on compliance requirements, system improvements, testing, and implementation follow-up.

Administrative Tasks (5%)

• Use spreadsheets, project management tools, and approved software to improve tracking, reporting, and organization.

• Support additional compliance initiatives assigned by the Compliance Officer, with final regulatory decisions and approvals remaining with authorized leadership.

Qualifications

Required

• High school diploma

• Minimum 2 years in compliance support, regulatory coordination, legal assistance/paralegal work, inspections, audits, or investigations.

• Minimum 2 years working in or supporting a regulated industry.

• Experience supporting compliance in a regulated environment through pharmacy operations, regulatory affairs, legal assistance/paralegal work, inspections, audits, or investigations.

• Advanced computer and technology proficiency, with the ability to work confidently across multiple software platforms and learn new systems quickly with minimal assistance.

• Strong Microsoft Office and Google Workspace skills, particularly Excel/Google Sheets, including formulas, filtering, data organization, and reporting.

• Experience using electronic document management, project tracking tools, digital forms, and collaboration platforms.

• Ability to research regulatory requirements using authoritative sources, review records, organize evidence, and prepare clear written summaries.

• Excellent organization and follow-through, including managing multiple projects, tracking deadlines, providing reminders, and escalating outstanding issues.

• Proactive, resourceful, and self-directed, with the ability to anticipate needs and complete delegated tasks with minimal supervision.

• Strong written and verbal English communication skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and discretion with confidential information.

• Ability to work across the Miami and Davie locations and accommodate occasional schedule changes or after-hours needs.

Preferred

• Pharmacy experience is strongly preferred. Relevant legal support, inspection, or investigation experience involving regulatory matters may qualify. These years may overlap with the similar-role requirement.

• Direct experience in pharmacy regulatory compliance, particularly community, mail-order, or compounding pharmacy operations.

• Familiarity with BOP requirements, FDA/DEA regulations, USP standards, or healthcare privacy requirements.

• Experience supporting SOP development, investigations, corrective actions, audits, and inspection preparation.

• Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in legal studies, healthcare administration, business, information systems, or a related field; paralegal or relevant compliance certification.

• Experience with pharmacy software, Atlassian tools, electronic training platforms, and workflow automation.

• Experience using approved AI tools responsibly, including verifying results and protecting confidential information.

• Bilingual English/Spanish.

Work Schedule

• Working out of both our Davie and Miami Gardens location

• Monday - Friday, 9AM to 6PM

Pay Range

$60,000—$66,000 USD

Benefits:

• 401(k) with up to 4% matching

• Medical, dental, vision and life insurance

• Paid time off that grows with your tenure

Core Values

The Pharmacy Hub is dedicated to breaking barriers in healthcare by championing access, intervention and affordability.

• Customer-first mindset - we develop strong partnerships with telehealth platforms and healthcare companies to enhance access and understand their specific needs

• Innovation for intervention in care - we develop advanced compounding solutions and products to better support patient health outcomes

• Continuous improvement - we continuously improve our processes and offerings through intelligent, honest and transparent practices to deliver cost-effective solutions that truly benefit our clients and their patients.

You will play a pivotal role in maintaining these values and contributing to the company’s mission of redefining healthcare delivery through superior pharmacy services

At The Pharmacy Hub, we don’t just offer jobs—we offer opportunities for career growth and development. We take pride in our fast-paced, team-driven culture and are committed to supporting our employees in achieving success.

If you’re ready to join a company that values hard work, dedication, and teamwork, apply today! We look forward to welcoming you to The Pharmacy Hub and working together to deliver top-tier pharmacy fulfillment solutions.

The Pharmacy Hub is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation to participate in the hiring process are encouraged to indicate this in their application.

The Pharmacy Hub participates in E-Verify. A post-offer background check is required for all positions. Additional pre-employment screenings may apply depending on the role.

jobs.title: Videographer, Scout Studios
jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Overview

Scout Studios is looking for a versatile Videographer who can move quickly, think visually, and take a story from idea to finish.

You'll help own the high-volume brand content pipeline that surrounds Scout's flagship storytelling, adding depth and character to the company’s story by capturing the people, vehicles, events, moments, and stories inside Scout Motors as the company continues to build.

One week you may be shooting a walkthrough at the Scout Motors Production Center in Blythewood, SC, the next, producing an experiential event recap, filming a product walkaround, supporting a CRM story, or off-roading in the desert, producing product development and adventure stories.

This role will be deeply embedded in the ongoing development of the Scout Motors company, brand, and vehicles, and is poised to own the content work that is quick, nimble, culturally aware, and often the most frequent interaction our audience will have with the Scout brand on our content channels.

You'll collaborate with the broader Scout Studios team while working directly with the Head of Scout Studios to develop a content and storytelling pipeline and creative identity of your own.

Why Scout Studios

Scout Motors and the Scout brand have a rare and special opportunity: we're building the company, the vehicles, the community, and the stories surrounding them from the ground up, at the same time.

Scout Studios has a front-row, all-access seat.

You'll help make sure the journey is told, from the large moments to the small stories in-between, that keep the momentum moving.

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

• Be a talented and visionary flex content creator.

• Shoot, edit, and deliver high-quality video content across Scout's digital ecosystem.

• Own projects from pitch and brief through capture, edit, finishing, and delivery.

• Drive short-form content across Scout’s online channels, with the goal of deepening our storytelling and entertainment content on our YouTube channel and other emerging platforms.

• Support CRM, corporate communications, internal communications, experience, and other cross-functional storytelling, while upholding Scout Studios’ creative and visual standards.

• Work with the Scout Studios team to capture interviews, product demonstrations, events, behind-the-scenes moments, employee stories, community stories, and lifestyle content.

• Lead creative approaches that elevate everyday content requests beyond traditional corporate video.

• Work comfortably as a solo creator when appropriate, operating cameras, lights, audio, directing, and editing.

• Scale up and collaborate with the larger Scout Studios crew for more ambitious productions.

• Work with the Head of Scout Studios to establish templates and repeatable production approaches for recurring content needs.

• Experiment with new formats, tools, technologies, and storytelling techniques.

Location & Travel Expectations:

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC.

• This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• This role will be embedded in the ongoing development of the Scout Motors company, brand, and vehicles. As such, travel will be a meaningful and necessary part of this role, with expected travel ranging from 40-50%.

• Scout vehicles are being developed for rugged adventure, worksite use, daily-living, and everything in-between, and candidates for this role should expect that travel will take them to a variety of climates and environments, including harsher cold-weather, hot-weather, mountainous, and remote locations.

• Candidates should be comfortable operating in remote and harsher conditions when necessary, and physically capable of carrying and operating equipment, from camera systems to lights and audio equipment as needed.

• Candidates for this position should carry an active drivers’ license, and be comfortable driving on urban, highway, and country roads, gravel roads, and some light off-road trails when needed.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• 5+ years of professional experience creating video and digital content.

• A portfolio demonstrating strong shooting, editing, and storytelling ability.

• A strong understanding of camera fundamentals including composition, exposure, movement, lenses, and lighting, and the ability to distinguish the right camera system for the right job.

• Strong proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Premiere Pro) and DaVinci Resolve.

• Understanding of modern social platforms and how storytelling changes between formats.

• Strong editorial instincts, pacing, music selection, and sound-design fundamentals.

• Ability to operate effectively as both a solo creator and part of a larger production crew.

• Strong organizational and file-management habits.

• Ability to work quickly while maintaining visual and brand standards.

• Curiosity and willingness to learn new tools and production techniques, and drive innovation.

• Minimum of High School Diploma, GED or equivalent required for all roles at Scout Motors, Inc.

Preferred

• Automotive or outdoor/lifestyle production experience.

• Photography experience.

• Drone certification and aerial-production experience.

• Motion graphics or After Effects experience.

• Color-grading experience.

• Experience producing social-first and vertical content.

• Experience with live events and fast-turn editorial.

• Experience working directly with executives, engineers, designers, craftspeople, or other nonprofessional on-camera talent.

• A strong passion for automotive culture, design, adventure, music, travel, or the outdoors.

Who You Are

You're a maker and a visionary.

When something interesting happens, your instinct is to figure out how to capture it and tell a story around it. You can see the story in a production center worker, an off-road adventure, an engineering prototype, a community gathering, or a thirty-second moment that most people might glance over.

You have a passion for driving the creative process from start to finish, diving deeper into stories, and enjoy operating both as a nimble solo-creator and part of a larger production crew.

You're curious, self-directed, collaborative, passionate about creating content, and eager to grow. You want ownership rather than simply receiving assignments.

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

• Competitive insurance including: Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans

• 401(k) program with: An employer match and immediate vesting

• Generous Paid Time Off including: 20 days planned PTO, as accrued 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $85,000.00 - $105,000.00

Internal leveling code: IC9

Notice to applicants:

• To be considered for career opportunities at Scout Motors, applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

• Residing in San Francisco: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

• Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

• Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

Equal Opportunity

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

When we succeed together, we share in that success. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Environmental Project Manager / Senior NEPA Specialist

The Environmental Project Manager / Senior NEPA Specialist leads environmental consulting projects across the energy, transmission, infrastructure, and transportation markets. This senior, client-facing position is responsible for technical delivery, project management, business development, client relationships, and team leadership. Responsibilities span opportunity development and project scoping through agency approval and project completion, with an additional focus on expanding Apex’s environmental consulting services in Central Oregon and the broader Northwest.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead environmental consulting projects from initiation through completion, including environmental assessments, NEPA reviews, permitting, compliance evaluations, industrial hygiene, indoor air quality, hazardous materials, and related services.

• Serve as environmental task manager on complex state- and federally funded projects, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, subconsultants, and agency partners to support design and construction.

• Develop and deliver EAs, EISs, programmatic reviews, permitting strategies, technical reports, work plans, corrective action plans, regulatory submittals, and other client deliverables.

• Lead environmental investigations and field activities, including site assessments, sampling, inspections, and data collection, in accordance with applicable regulations and industry standards.

• Evaluate field and laboratory data and develop practical recommendations that address environmental, health and safety, regulatory, and client needs.

• Manage scope, schedule, budget, contracts, risk, and quality across complex engagements.

• Serve as the primary client contact and advisor and independently scope, price, negotiate, and defend proposed work.

• Coordinate subcontractors, laboratories, field staff, and other resources to deliver projects safely and efficiently.

• Develop and maintain relationships with federal, state, local, and utility decision-makers; prepare proposals and presentations; and pursue sole-source and follow-on work.

• Mentor project managers and technical staff and provide hands-on guidance for fieldwork, analysis, and report preparation.

• Collaborate with environmental scientists, industrial hygienists, engineers, architects, contractors, and facility managers.

• Help grow Apex’s environmental and NEPA practice in Central Oregon and the Northwest while contributing to firm-wide market strategy.

• Stay current on environmental regulations, emerging issues, industry standards, and best management practices.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, environmental health and safety, industrial hygiene, or a related field.

• Eight plus years of relevant environmental consulting experience, including at least seven years focused on NEPA with substantial federal experience.

• Demonstrated success managing projects end to end, including scope, schedule, budget, contracts, client communication, regulatory coordination, quality, and delivery risk.

• Experience preparing and delivering NEPA documentation and working successfully with federal, state, and local agency environmental staff.

• Experience with environmental assessments, regulatory compliance, hazardous materials, industrial hygiene, indoor air quality, natural resources, environmental permitting, or related services.

• Working knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations, including OSHA and EPA requirements.

• Strong technical writing, project management, problem-solving, leadership, and client communication skills.

• Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, priorities, and client relationships with accountability and sound judgment.

• Demonstrated ability to develop client relationships, originate opportunities, and manage both sales and project delivery responsibilities.

• Commitment to safe work practices and effective leadership of field and office teams.

• Valid driver’s license with a good driving record.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and standard environmental data management, project management, and reporting tools.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Oregon environmental regulations, agencies, and permitting processes; Washington, California, or comparable jurisdictional experience will also be considered.

• Familiarity with permitting and agency coordination related to wetlands, waters, habitat, land use, and other resource-protection programs.

• Established client and agency relationships in the Northwest United States and a record of securing repeat, sole-source, or follow-on work.

• Experience shaping or growing a NEPA or environmental consulting practice.

• Professional certification such as CIH, CSP, CEM, CPESC, or another relevant environmental credential.

Why you'll love working for us:

• Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.

• 401k match, tuition assistance, and more.

• Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.

Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee?
